hittite_arinna.name: Grant kingship and victory in war
hittite_arinna.notes: As source of royal legitimacy she runs before the Hittite king in battle and grants him victory; the king and queen serve as her high priest and priestess.

sources.reference: Prayer of Mursili II to the Sun-goddess of Arinna (CTH 376)

hittite_arinna.name: Govern the established order of heaven and earth
hittite_arinna.notes: Invoked as Queen of Heaven and Earth who sets the bounds of kingship and law for the Land of Hatti.

sources.reference: Prayer of Mursili II to the Sun-goddess of Arinna (CTH 376)

hittite_tarhunna.name: Command thunder, lightning, and rain
hittite_tarhunna.notes: The Storm-god of Hatti wields the thunderbolt and brings the rains on which the land's fertility depends.

sources.reference: Hittite state treaties and royal prayers (CTH series)

hittite_tarhunna.name: Slay the chaos-serpent Illuyanka
hittite_tarhunna.notes: After an initial defeat, he destroys the dragon Illuyanka with the help of his daughter Inara (first version) or his half-mortal son (second version), recovering his stolen heart and eyes.

sources.reference: Illuyanka myth (CTH 321), recited at the purulli festival

hittite_tarhunna.name: Guarantee oaths and treaties as divine witness
hittite_tarhunna.notes: Named as chief witness and enforcer in Hittite state treaties, who destroys the perjurer.

sources.reference: Treaty of Suppiluliuma I with Shattiwaza (CTH 51)

hittite_telipinu.name: Grant fertility to crops, herds, and people
hittite_telipinu.notes: His presence sustains the growth of grain, the increase of cattle and sheep, and human birth; his withdrawal blights all three.

hittite_telipinu.name: Withdraw in anger and wither the land
hittite_telipinu.notes: The archetypal vanishing god: enraged, he storms off (putting his boots on the wrong feet) so that mist seizes the hearth and fields and springs dry up until he is found and soothed.

hittite_inara.name: Mistress of the wild creatures of the steppe
hittite_inara.notes: Hattic-derived goddess of the wild animals, daughter of the Storm-god, comparable to a potnia theron.

hittite_inara.name: Entrap the serpent through cunning and feasting
hittite_inara.notes: Stages a great feast to make Illuyanka and his brood drunk, then has the mortal Hupasiya bind them so the Storm-god can slay the dragon.

hittite_illuyanka.name: Overpower the Storm-god and seize his heart and eyes
hittite_illuyanka.notes: In the second version the serpent bests Tarhunna in their first combat and takes his heart and eyes as spoils before the god recovers them.

hittite_hannahanna.name: Dispatch the bee to find the vanished god
hittite_hannahanna.notes: The Grandmother resolves the disappearing-god crises by sending a bee to locate the lost deity, sting him awake, and purify him with wax.

hittite_hannahanna.name: Preside over childbirth and decree destiny
hittite_hannahanna.notes: Primeval mother- and birth-goddess (identified with Nintu) associated with the Gulses goddesses of fate.

sources.reference: Hittite ritual and cult texts invoking Ḫannaḫanna with the Gulses

hittite_mezzulla.name: Intercede with the Sun-goddess of Arinna
hittite_mezzulla.notes: Daughter of the Storm-god and the Sun-goddess of Arinna; conveys mortal prayers to her powerful mother as a divine intermediary.

sources.reference: Hittite royal prayers and the cult of Arinna (CTH series)

hittite_zintuhi.name: Intercede with the Sun-goddess of Arinna
hittite_zintuhi.notes: Granddaughter of the Sun-goddess and the Storm-god (her name is Hattic for granddaughter); like her mother Mezzulla, invoked as an intermediary with the Sun-goddess.

sources.reference: Hittite cult texts of Arinna (CTH series)

hindu_vishrava.name: Mastery of Vedic learning won through tapas
hindu_vishrava.notes: A scholar par excellence among the rishis, he gained great powers and renown through austerity (tapasya).

hindu_vishrava.name: Progenitor of the rakshasa and yaksha lines
hindu_vishrava.notes: By Ilavida he fathered Kubera, and by Kaikasi he fathered Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha, and Vibhishana.

hindu_vyasa.name: Divide and arrange the Vedas into four collections
hindu_vyasa.notes: Traditionally compiled the single body of Vedic mantras into the Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva, earning the title Vyasa ('the arranger').

hindu_vyasa.name: Compose the Mahabharata and the Puranas
hindu_vyasa.notes: Author of the Mahabharata (dictated to Ganesha) and traditionally of the eighteen Puranas and the Brahma Sutras.

hindu_vyasa.name: Deathless sage of the present age
hindu_vyasa.notes: Counted among the Chiranjivis (immortals) and regarded as a partial incarnation (amsavatara) of Vishnu.

hindu_vinata.name: Mother of the solar charioteer and the king of birds
hindu_vinata.notes: By Kashyapa she bore two eggs that hatched Aruna (charioteer of Surya and personification of dawn) and Garuda (mount of Vishnu).

hindu_vinata.name: Loses the wager and falls into bondage
hindu_vinata.notes: Wagers with her sister Kadru over the color of Uchchaihshravas' tail; deceived, she becomes Kadru's slave until freed when Garuda fetches the amrita.

hindu_yudhishthira.name: Answer the questions of the Yaksha (Dharma)
hindu_yudhishthira.notes: At the lake in exile he alone answers the Yaksha's riddles correctly, reviving his fallen brothers; the Yaksha is his father Dharma in disguise.

hindu_yudhishthira.name: Ascend to heaven in his mortal body with the dog
hindu_yudhishthira.notes: Refusing to abandon the dog that followed him, he is taken bodily into Svarga; the dog is revealed as Dharma testing him.

sources.reference: Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva and Svargarohana Parva

hindu_vishnu_varaha.name: Plunge to the floor of the cosmic ocean
hindu_vishnu_varaha.notes: Dives into the waters that had submerged the earth to seek the lost Bhumi.

sources.reference: Hittite and Hurro-Hittite storm-god iconography (e.g. relief depictions)
Hittite cult inventories and storm-god iconography

hittite_telipinu.name: Eya-tree (evergreen) hung with the fleece-bag of abundance

sources.reference: Iconography of Vyasa in Hindu tradition

hittite_tarhunna.original: Lord of the Land of Hatti

hittite_tudhaliya_iv.gloss: My Sun (royal title of the Hittite Great King)

hittite_suppiluliuma_ii.gloss: My Sun (royal title of the Hittite Great King)

sources.reference: Südburg hieroglyphic inscription; Hittite royal titulary

hindu_vyasa.gloss: the dark one born on an island
he of the jujube (badara) island; author of the Brahma Sutras

hittite_arinna.name: State cult of the Sun-goddess at Arinna
hittite_arinna.notes: Principal state deity whose temple at the holy city Arinna received royal offerings; the king and queen served as her chief priest and priestess and she was given the spoils of victory.

sources.reference: Hittite cult inventories and royal prayers (CTH 376)

hittite_tarhunna.name: Purulli new-year festival
hittite_tarhunna.notes: Spring new-year festival celebrating the Storm-god's victory over Illuyanka, at which the dragon-slaying myth was recited to renew the land's fertility.

hittite_telipinu.name: Disappearing-god appeasement ritual
hittite_telipinu.notes: Mugawar ritual of soothing: honey, fine oil, and libations with incantations to draw the angry god back and restore fertility; honored with a great festival at Hanhana and Kasha.

hittite_hannahanna.name: Invocation in birth and disappearing-god rituals
hittite_hannahanna.notes: Invoked in domestic ritual texts for childbirth and infant protection and in the mugawar rites to send the bee after the vanished deity.

hittite_mezzulla.name: Worship in the Arinna triad
hittite_mezzulla.notes: Worshipped beside her mother in a dedicated temple at Arinna (second in importance after the Sun-goddess's), receiving libations and bread offerings at the monthly festival.

hindu_vishnu_narasimha.name: Narasimha Jayanti
hindu_vishnu_narasimha.notes: Celebrated on Vaishakha shukla chaturdashi (April–May), marking the deity's appearance at twilight; performed as Bhagavata Mela dance-drama in Tamil Nadu and centered on the nine-fold shrine complex of Ahobilam.

sources.reference: Narasimha Jayanti and Ahobilam temple tradition

hindu_vishwakarma.name: Vishvakarma Puja
hindu_vishwakarma.notes: Worship of the divine craftsman (mid-September), in which artisans, engineers, and workers venerate their tools and machinery.

hindu_yama.name: Yama Dwitiya (Bhai Dooj)
hindu_yama.notes: On the second day after Diwali, sisters honor brothers and offer arghya and lamps to Yama to avert untimely death (apamrityu); tarpana is offered to him with his fourteen names.

hindu_vyasa.name: Guru Purnima (Vyasa Purnima)
hindu_vyasa.notes: The full-moon of Ashadha is observed as Guru Purnima honoring Vyasa as the adi-guru and compiler of the Vedas.

hochunk_disease_giver.name: Offerings in the war-bundle ceremony
hochunk_disease_giver.notes: Honored among the great spirits of the war-bundle feast alongside Earthmaker, the Thunderbirds, and the Night Spirits; dogs were sacrificed to him as messengers in time of need.

hochunk_hare.name: The Medicine Rite (Medicine Lodge)
hochunk_hare.notes: Founder-hero of the Ho-Chunk Medicine Rite, the secret society and rebirth ceremony whose foundation myth recounts his works and his Grandmother's ordaining of death.

sources.reference: Paul Radin, The Road of Life and Death (1945)

attributes.name: Winged sun-disk
attributes.notes: Symbolized by the solar disk and winged sun emblem; cult inventories describe her as a golden sun-disk and as a seated female statue receiving offerings.

attributes.name: Standing on the mountain-gods Namni and Hazzi
attributes.notes: Depicted as a bearded man in a pointed cap, brandishing the thunderbolt, striding on the backs of the deified mountains.

sources.reference: Hittite storm-god iconography; silver bull dedicated to his temple

attributes.name: Bursting from the pillar
attributes.notes: Shown emerging from a split column at the threshold, signifying his omnipresence, as he seizes Hiranyakashipu across his lap to disembowel him with his claws while Prahlada looks on.

attributes.name: Lion head on a human body
attributes.notes: Lion's face with mane and fangs, clawed hands, on a man's body; depicted in the seated Yoga, fierce Ugra, and Lakshmi-accompanied forms.

attributes.name: Earth-goddess raised on the tusk
attributes.notes: Theriomorphic or boar-headed form lifting Bhumi/Bhudevi on his right tusk, often in the warrior's alidha stance with a naga in submission at his feet, as at Udayagiri Cave 5 and the Khajuraho Varaha.

sources.reference: Udayagiri Cave 5 relief; Khajuraho Varaha temple

attributes.name: Measuring scale, book, and water-pot
attributes.notes: Commonly an aged white-bearded craftsman with four arms holding a measuring scale or tape, a book, and a kamandalu; in eastern India shown as a young muscular figure.

attributes.name: Dark-green or red form with noose and rod
attributes.notes: Depicted with a dark or green complexion, red garments, holding the danda (rod of punishment) and pasha (noose) with which he draws out the soul.

attributes.name: Shaper of the first human from clay
attributes.notes: In Radin's origin myth he wakes alone in space, his tears form the primal waters, and he molds the first man from clay in his own likeness, giving tobacco as his gift.

attributes.name: Hunched flute-player with insect antennae
attributes.notes: Humpbacked figure playing a flute, often shown with antenna-like protrusions linking him to the locust/insect; his hump is a sack of seeds and rain-bringing mist, and he is said to carry unborn children for women.

attributes.name: Skull-faced mask (Skeleton Man)
attributes.notes: Wears a fearsome mask whose face is a skull blotched with cloud-marks and crowned with prayer feathers; alternately revealed as a handsome bejewelled man beneath the mask.

sources.reference: Hopi mythology and katsina iconography of Maasaw

attributes.name: Sky-giant standing astride, looking down on all
attributes.notes: Imagined as an enormous high-god who stands with legs astride above the world and watches all humans, punishing breaches of kinship law; he is set apart from the dama spirits and cannot be swayed by ritual.

sources.reference: R. M. Glasse, Huli of Papua (1968)
